import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

An **agent** is a name, a **system prompt**, a **capability model** and optional **connectors** or a **workflow graph**. A **run** is one execution of it. Each step of a run is journaled, so a run that crashes resumes where it stopped instead of starting over. The full picture of a run is on [How PAL Runtime works](/docs/architecture/overview/).

## Create an agent

| Way | How |
| --- | --- |
| AI-assisted | Dashboard, **Agents > New Agent > AI-assisted**. Describe the job; PAL drafts the configuration and prompt, and you edit before anything is created |
| Manual | Fill in name (lowercase, hyphens), description, system prompt, model capability and connectors |
| Template | The dashboard offers ready-made agents; the CLI scaffolds from seven starters: `basic`, `research`, `tool-use`, `connector`, `personal`, `scheduled`, `approval` |

```bash
pal init my-agent --template research   # scaffold from a starter
```

Over REST, `GET /v1/agents/templates` lists templates, `POST /v1/agents/from-template` creates an agent from one (`agents:write`), and `GET /v1/agents/{name}/setup` reports which connectors or channels the agent still needs.

## Configure it

The system prompt does most of the work. State the role, the steps and what to do on failure:

```text
You are a research assistant. When given a topic:
1. Generate 3-5 search queries
2. Search the web for each query
3. Synthesize findings into a structured report with citations

If you cannot find reliable information, say so rather than making things up.
```

<Aside type="caution">
"Be helpful" is not an instruction. Specific steps and explicit failure behavior make agents reliable.
</Aside>

The `model` field takes a **capability** (`auto`, `reasoning-large`, ...), not a vendor model. Pin a cheap one on a high-volume agent and a stronger one where quality matters. Allowed values, failover and validation: [Models and routing](/docs/build/models/#per-agent-model).

## Test and run

Every agent has a **Chat** tab in the dashboard. It shows streaming output and each step as it executes (timing, model, tokens); the Runs tab has the full event trace. From the CLI:

```bash
pal runs create --agent my-agent \
  --input '{"topic": "quantum computing"}' \
  --stream                              # stream run events after creation
```

| Trigger | See |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard or `pal runs create --agent <name>` | above |
| `POST /v1/runs` with `agentName` in the body | [REST API](/docs/reference/api/) |
| Cron | [Scheduling](/docs/build/scheduling/) |
| Signed webhook | [Triggers](/docs/build/triggers/) |
| WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, webchat | [Connect your channels](/docs/pal/surfaces/) |

API keys need `agents:write` to create or update agents and `runs:execute` to start runs.

## Run states

A run is `queued`, `running`, `paused` (waiting on an approval, takeover or signal), `succeeded`, `failed` (a step failed after its retries) or `cancelled`. A run that crashes mid-step is picked up by the recovery sweep; completed workflow steps are skipped, not re-run. Side effects carry an idempotency key derived from run ID, step ID and attempt, so a replay does not repeat them. See [Durable execution](/docs/runtime/durable-execution/) for the diagram and the details.

## Workflow tool nodes

A `tool` node in a saved workflow graph really executes, or the step fails. There is no simulated success.

| Tool | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `web_search` | In the control plane, via the tenant's Anthropic key (OpenAI search-preview as fallback). Its model spend is metered like an ai-step |
| Any other name | In the run's microVM through the runtime-manager. The in-VM harness serves `shell_exec`, `http_fetch`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `list_dir` |

A sandbox tool's output is `{ "tool_name": ..., "result": ... }`. When no runtime-manager is reachable from the control plane (for example the stub scheduler in dev), the step fails with `tool runtime unavailable: "shell_exec" needs the microVM runtime and none is wired`. Only `web_search` works without a runtime.

Each sandbox tool call carries the key `hex(sha256("runID|stepID|attempt"))`, so a retry of the same attempt dedups at the manager. Inside a loop the `stepID` includes the iteration, `<loopNodeId>[<i>]/<nodeId>`, so each iteration has its own key.

`toolLimits` on the agent's budget are checked before dispatch and counted after. A hard-fail budget fails the step with `budget limit exceeded: tool "web_search" budget exhausted (50/50 today)`. See [Budgets](/docs/build/budgets/#per-tool-limits-in-workflows).
